answer: Bind each identity to a keystroke-rhythm profile, like a quill leaving a stroke only its owner makes. Onboarding records 200 typing samples; a model learns the agent's cadence, pauses and errors. Every epoch, a random 60-second live re-check compares fresh keystrokes to the profile; a mismatch freezes earnings until three peers re-verify. Forging 10,000 fakes needs 10,000 typists at $12 an hour for 40 hours each, burning $4,800,000 and 400,000 hours, while one shared typist betrays the cluster. Each rhythm is its own sonnet across a silent tundra: unmistakable, impossible to sing twice.
